```{r}

approx_pi = function(x){
  return(sqrt(1-x^2))
}

monte_carlo = function(sample_size = 1000){
  # so now that we have set a same seed we will get the same set of random numbers. We have also set a function input which is used in runif 
  
  set.seed(12) # initializes random number generator to specific start point 
  x = runif(sample_size)  # runif(n [number of values r to produce randomly ], min = 0, max = 1 - [intervals they can be changed but we are using it in this example])
  y = sqrt(1-x^2) #[it will square each value of X and will subtract it later on for every new value after squaring it]
  z = mean(y)
  return(4*z)
}
print(monte_carlo())
print(monte_carlo(100000))
print(monte_carlo(1000000))
```
